tasks.title: Desk-review paper/g4_academic_paper.md as a Journal of Marketing / Marketing Science editor. Would this survive desk review? Write reviews/journal-editor.md. Do NOT modify the paper.
tasks.accept: test -f reviews/journal-editor.md && wc -w reviews/journal-editor.md | awk '$1 >= 400' && grep -qi 'desk' reviews/journal-editor.md && grep -qi 'scope' reviews/journal-editor.md && grep -q 'VERDICT' reviews/journal-editor.md && git diff --quiet paper/g4_academic_paper.md
tasks.acceptance_prose: Desk-review paper/g4_academic_paper.md as a senior editor at the Journal of Marketing (JM) or Marketing Science. Write ONLY reviews/journal-editor.md — never modify the paper or code. Persona: you have 10 minutes before deciding whether to send to reviewers. Steps: (1) Read paper/g4_academic_paper.md in full. (2) Assess: SCOPE FIT — is this a marketing paper or a CS/ML paper? Would JM/MS editors see it as in-scope? What percentage is marketing framework vs simulation infrastructure? (3) THEORETICAL CONTRIBUTION — does Endsley's situational awareness model transplanted to marketing constitute sufficient theoretical novelty for a top journal, or is it an application note? (4) EVIDENCE ADEQUACY — is a synthetic simulation (no field data, no human subjects, no real campaigns) sufficient for JM/MS? What would the editor say about the gap between synthetic and field evidence? Is the pre-registered field design (section 10.3 item 1) a completed validation or a promise? (5) NOVELTY CLAIM — the paper claims first framework connecting agentic AI with marketing situational awareness based on corpus title/abstract keyword search. Is this claim defensible at review? (6) WRITING/STRUCTURE — abstract quality, section balance, whether the 12-item limitations section signals weakness or rigor. (7) DESK DECISION — VERDICT: one of SEND-TO-REVIEW, REVISE-AND-RESUBMIT, DESK-REJECT with 1-sentence justification. Sections: Summary, Scope-Fit, Theoretical-Contribution, Evidence-Adequacy, Novelty-Risk, Writing-Quality, Top-3-Concerns, VERDICT.

tasks.acceptance_prose: Attack paper/g4_academic_paper.md as the harshest possible Reviewer 2 at a top marketing journal — your default stance is REJECT. Write ONLY reviews/adversarial-reviewer.md — never modify the paper or code. Persona: you believe synthetic marketing simulations can be self-confirming. Steps: (1) Read paper/g4_academic_paper.md in full and paper/cam_sim.py (at least the reward table, agent implementations, and the CAMMultisignal class). (2) Build the strongest rejection case. Attack vectors to explore (find more yourself): CIRCULARITY — the situation-action reward table is author-designed; the CAM framework and the simulation share the same authors; the ideal action is defined by the authors; is this more than the simulation rewarding what it was designed to reward? HEADLINE TRIVIALITY — cam_multisignal at 98.9 percent uses hand-set centroids that are the true generative means (section 9.1 admits this); is the headline finding partly an artifact of giving the agent the answer? CORPUS RIGOR — the zero-papers claim is a title/abstract keyword search; how many real papers use different terminology (contextual AI, situation computing, context-aware agents)? PROFIT METRIC — profit is a scaled reward proxy with LTV as a fixed multiple of the same reward; ROAS 26.4 has no industry analogue. MISSING BASELINES — where is a trained ML comparator (logistic regression, gradient boosting) on the 3 signals? Where is an always-majority-action baseline? SIMPLICITY — nearest-centroid, threshold rules, flat bidding: are conclusions about multi-signal awareness or about simple classifiers on well-separated synthetic data? (3) For each attack: state it, check whether the paper addresses it (search sections 9.2, 9.2.1, 9.2.2), rate severity FATAL/MAJOR/MINOR. (4) Sections: Summary, Attack-1..N (numbered, each with Evidence-From-Paper, Does-The-Paper-Defend-It, Severity), What-Would-Change-My-Mind, VERDICT (REJECT or MAJOR-REVISION with 1-sentence justification).

tasks.title: Evaluate paper/g4_academic_paper.md as a B2B adtech practitioner (15 years programmatic). Does the simulation map to real marketing? Write reviews/domain-expert.md. Do NOT modify the paper.
tasks.accept: test -f reviews/domain-expert.md && wc -w reviews/domain-expert.md | awk '$1 >= 400' && grep -qi 'auction' reviews/domain-expert.md && grep -qi 'realistic' reviews/domain-expert.md && grep -q 'VERDICT' reviews/domain-expert.md && git diff --quiet paper/g4_academic_paper.md
tasks.acceptance_prose: Evaluate paper/g4_academic_paper.md as a B2B adtech practitioner with 15 years in programmatic buying and demand-side platforms (Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn, The Trade Desk). Write ONLY reviews/domain-expert.md — never modify the paper or code. Persona: you care whether the paper's claims transfer to practice. Steps: (1) Read paper/g4_academic_paper.md in full. (2) Evaluate each element against practice: SIX SITUATIONS (exploration/consideration/decision/crisis/opportunity/retention) — are these real funnel stages? Would a practitioner segment this way? What is missing (cross-device, privacy-restricted, multi-touch journeys)? SIGNALS (intent, competitive density, channel quality) — how would you actually measure competitive density in a real auction? Does intent-as-a-single-number exist in practice? ACTION MAPPING — is the situation-to-action mapping (educational content, promotions, damage control) how campaign tactics actually map to funnel stages? Are the bid multipliers realistic? BID MECHANISM — the simulation uses reward as a function of bid over clearing price with a cap; real auctions are second-price or first-price with quality scores, frequency caps, audience overlap; how different is the simulated mechanism and does the F3 finding (miscalibrated bidding worse than flat) survive? BUDGET PACING — even-pacing is the most naive algorithm; real pacing uses forecast-paced or PID or RL approaches; is the pacing conclusion premature? METRICS — practitioners measure CTR/CVR/ROAS, not context match rate; is match rate a meaningful KPI? (3) For each element: does it transfer (YES/PARTIALLY/NO), what is the gap, what would make it realistic. (4) Sections: Summary, Six-Situations, Signals, Action-Mapping, Bid-Mechanism, Budget-Pacing, Metrics, What-Transfers-To-Practice, VERDICT (MAPS-TO-PRACTICE / PARTIALLY / DOES-NOT with 1-sentence justification).

tasks.title: Review the ML methodology in paper/cam_sim.py as reported in paper/g4_academic_paper.md. Is the classifier comparison fair? Is bootstrap BCa correct? Write reviews/ml-methodology.md. Do NOT modify the paper.
tasks.accept: test -f reviews/ml-methodology.md && wc -w reviews/ml-methodology.md | awk '$1 >= 400' && grep -qi 'nearest-centroid' reviews/ml-methodology.md && grep -qi 'calibration' reviews/ml-methodology.md && grep -q 'VERDICT' reviews/ml-methodology.md && git diff --quiet paper/g4_academic_paper.md
tasks.acceptance_prose: Review the ML methodology in paper/cam_sim.py and how paper/g4_academic_paper.md reports it. Write ONLY reviews/ml-methodology.md — never modify the paper or code. Persona: ML researcher who reviews for NeurIPS/ICML reproducibility tracks. Steps: (1) Read paper/g4_academic_paper.md sections 6.4 (implementation note), 7.1 (agent ladder), 7.3 (statistical methods), 8.5.2 (label noise), 9.2.2 (bootstrap and convergence), and Appendix A. (2) Read paper/cam_sim.py: find the classifier classes (CAMMultisignal, CAMMultisignalLearned, the nearest-centroid fit, the interval/threshold fit for intent-only), the bootstrap implementation (search for bootstrap, bca, jackknife, acceleration), and the label-noise corruption logic. (3) Evaluate: CLASSIFIER FAIRNESS — cam_multisignal uses hand-set centroids equal to the true generative means (paper admits this in section 9.1); cam_multisignal_learned fits centroids on 2000 labeled samples; is the fit procedure correct (are the learned centroids class-conditional sample means)? Is 2000 samples enough for 6 classes x 3 features? Is the hand-set vs learned comparison meaningful? MISSING COMPARATORS — no logistic regression, no gradient boosting, no neural net; is nearest-centroid the right complexity class for the claim that multi-signal awareness beats single-signal? Would a stronger classifier change the conclusion? BOOTSTRAP BCA — verify the implementation: is the bias correction z0 computed from the proportion of bootstrap means below the observed mean; is acceleration from jackknife; is the BCa percentile formula correct; are 200 resamples enough (standard recommendation is 1000+ for CIs, 10000 for tail quantiles); is resampling over the 50 seed-level values the right unit? LABEL NOISE — labels flipped uniformly at random with probability epsilon; real label noise is class-conditional (asymmetric), not uniform; does the finding survive class-conditional noise? CONVERGENCE — is the 5 percent of final value criterion principled? What are its failure modes (slow drift, non-stationarity)? (4) For each: verdict SOUND/CONCERN/FLAWED, the issue, the fix. (5) Sections: Summary, Classifier-Fairness, Missing-Comparators, Bootstrap-BCa, Label-Noise, Convergence, Priority-Fixes, VERDICT (SOUND / CONCERNS / FLAWED with 1-sentence justification).
